A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
RR Lyrae star data are consistent with the picture that the Galactic halo has a metallicity gradient, with a mean metallicity that increases toward the Galactic center.

the stellar halo of the Galaxy is a complex, inhomogeneous system, in which a significant fraction of stars is associated with substructure, and the metallicity of stars varies significantly from one clump to another, and from one region to another.
the outer halo is more complex, more metal-rich, and has a steeper number density profile than the inner halo, but the metal-poor inner halo is not completely smooth.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the outer-halo population, which is not dominated by any single accreted substructure, is more metal-poor on average than the inner halo, but is more metal-rich than a smooth, early-forming, metal-poor inner halo.
RR Lyrae are a powerful tracer of the outer halo, but their use as a tracer of the inner-halo metallicity distribution is limited by their metallicity sensitivity.

RR Lyrae light curve templates, and the RR Lyrae selection based on them, are powerful tools to identify substructure in the outer halo, and to study the properties of halo substructure, including its metallicity distribution.
